### 1.1 Code Analysis

Looking at the provided `pyproject.toml`:
- Uses standard project configuration with name, version, dependencies
- Has an optional dependency group `inner` with a git-based dependency
- Has a `dependency-groups` section with `editable-inner` containing a local editable file dependency
- Uses `${PROJECT_ROOT}` variable substitution in the editable path

### 1.2 Technical Details Highlighted

**Error Message**: `file:///${PROJECT_ROOT}/../config-resolver#egg=config-resolver: Editable requirement is only supported for VCS link or local directory.`

**Stack Trace Key Methods**:
- `pdm/installers/base.py` line 96 - iterating through `self.environment.project.all_dependencies.values()`
- `pdm/project/core.py` line 457 - `all_dependencies` property 
- `pdm/project/core.py` line 441 - `get_dependencies` method
- `pdm/models/requirements.py` line 528 - `parse_requirement` function

**Command**: `pdm sync --prod -G inner`

### 1.3 Problem Explanation

PDM 2.22.2 introduced a regression where the system parses ALL dependency groups (including those not requested) during installation/sync operations. When running `pdm sync --prod -G inner`, it should only process the "inner" group, but instead it also tries to parse the "editable-inner" group. Since the editable dependency uses a local file path that doesn't exist in the CI environment, it fails.

### 1.4 Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a `pyproject.toml` with both regular and editable dependency groups
2. Include an editable dependency that references a local path (`file:///${PROJECT_ROOT}/...`)
3. Run `pdm sync --prod -G <specific-group>` specifying only one group
4. Observe that PDM tries to parse all groups, including the unrequested editable group
5. Get a failure when it can't resolve the local editable dependency

### 1.5 Best Practices for Testing and Fixing

- Focus on the dependency resolution logic that determines which groups to parse
- Ensure the fix respects the group selection specified in CLI commands
- Test both scenarios: when groups are included vs excluded
- Verify backward compatibility with existing functionality

27 28 ## What is PDM? 29 30 PDM is meant to be a next generation Python package management tool. 31 It was originally built for personal use. If you feel you are going well 32 with `Pipenv` or `Poetry` and don't want to introduce another package manager, 33 just stick to it. But if you are missing something that is not present in those tools, 34 you can probably find some goodness in `pdm`. 35 36 ## Highlights of features 37 38 - Simple and fast dependency resolver, mainly for large binary distributions. 39 - A [PEP 517] build backend. 40 - [PEP 621] project metadata. 41 - Flexible and powerful plug-in system. 42 - Versatile user scripts. 43 - Install Pythons using [indygreg's python-build-standalone](https://github.com/indygreg/python-build-standalone). 44 - Opt-in centralized installation cache like [pnpm](https://pnpm.io/motivation#saving-disk-space-and-boosting-installation-speed). 45 46 [pep 517]: https://www.python.org/dev/peps/pep-0517 47 [pep 621]: https://www.python.org/dev/peps/pep-0621 48 [pnpm]: https://pnpm.io/motivation#saving-disk-space-and-boosting-installation-speed 49 50 ## Comparisons to other alternatives 51 52 ### [Pipenv](https://pipenv.pypa.io) 53 54 Pipenv is a dependency manager that combines `pip` and `venv`, as the name implies. 55 It can install packages from a non-standard `Pipfile.lock` or `Pipfile`. 56 However, Pipenv does not handle any packages related to packaging your code, 57 so it’s useful only for developing non-installable applications (Django sites, for example). 58 If you’re a library developer, you need `setuptools` anyway. 59 60 ### [Poetry](https://python-poetry.org) 61 62 Poetry manages environments and dependencies in a similar way to Pipenv, 63 but it can also build .whl files with your code, and it can upload wheels and source distributions to PyPI. 64 It has a pretty user interface and users can customize it via a plugin. Poetry uses the `pyproject.toml` standard, 65 but it does not follow the standard specifying how metadata should be represented in a pyproject.toml file ([PEP 621]), 66 instead using a custom `[tool.poetry]` table. This is partly because Poetry came out before PEP 621. 67 68 ### [Hatch](https://hatch.pypa.io) 69 70 Hatch can also manage environments, allowing multiple environments per project. By default it has a central location for all environments but it can be configured to put a project's environment(s) in the project root directory. It can manage packages but without lockfile support. It can also be used to package a project (with PEP 621 compliant pyproject.toml files) and upload it to PyPI. 71 72 ### This project 73 74 PDM can manage virtual environments (venvs) in both project and centralized locations, similar to Pipenv. It reads project metadata from a standardized `pyproject.toml` file and supports lockfiles. Users can add additional functionality through plugins, which can be shared by uploading them as distributions. 75 76 Unlike Poetry and Hatch, PDM is not limited to a specific build backend; users have the freedom to choose any build backend they prefer. 77 78 ## Installation 79 80 81 82 83 84 PDM requires python version 3.9 or higher. 85 86 ### Via Install Script 87 88 Like Pip, PDM provides
